phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Implementation Contract Independent Verification
summary: Phase 147F independently reconstructed the implementation-level requirements for pcae.authority_evaluation from AEM-001 v1.0, Phase 147C's independent verification, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, CHGR-001, TAMC-001/TAMPC-001, GAC-001, the Decision Template and Human Governance Record schemas, and direct re-inspection of src/pcae/interactive_workflow/models/session.py, src/pcae/governance/publication/{coordinator.py,record.py}, and tests/test_phase_144c_publication_coordinator.py's AST-enforced forbidden-import boundary -- treating Phase 147D's own implementation architecture strictly as non-authoritative design evidence before opening AEMIC-001 v1.0 itself. The independent reconstruction agrees with AEMIC-001 on package boundary and forbidden-import direction, disclosure-only semantics, Registry read-only/duplicate/availability semantics, identity/versioning rules, serialization rules, persistence deferral, and the deferred-integration boundary. Discovered and confirmed by direct textual attack a single Blocking finding (BF-147F-1): AEMIC-001's evaluate() function is frozen with a closed, exactly-four-parameter signature (claimed_identity, declaration, evaluated_at, evaluator_version -- AEMIC-REQ-019/020/072), and EligibleAuthorityDeclaration is frozen to exactly six fields, none of them citation_text (AEMIC-REQ-015/016), yet AEMIC-REQ-022 requires every eligible-result AuthorityEvaluationOutcome to carry a non-None citation_text, enforced 'at construction time, not left to caller discipline,' with evaluate() as the contract's sole specified construction path (Sec.14). No well-formed call to evaluate() satisfies both the closed-parameter rule and the citation invariant simultaneously for the eligible case; AEMIC-REQ-031's own text asserts, self-contradictorily, that Declarations copy citation text into the outcome at evaluation time while confirming in the same paragraph that no such field or parameter exists. The security-relevant consequence: a real implementation would need to bypass evaluate() entirely to construct an eligible outcome, defeating the citation invariant's own stated purpose of foreclosing caller-controlled citation fabrication. Four inherited findings (F-147C-1, F-147C-2, FA-147D-1, FA-147D-2, FA-147D-3) were independently re-derived from primary sources; four are reconfirmed accurate as AEMIC-001 characterizes them, and F-147C-1's 'reconciled' characterization is now qualified by BF-147F-1. Two Non-Blocking observations are newly disclosed (Unicode-normalization identity matching; the existing coordinator forbidden-import test not yet extended to name the new package). This phase reports BF-147F-1; it does not amend AEMIC-001's own text, consistent with the governing prompt's explicit instruction to report, not repair, a discovered defect. Verdict: NOT VERIFIED. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147F_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md.
